extracted.intended_audience: subjects and readers of a Christian commonwealth; those who must judge claims of prophecy and miracles
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria (scriptural, rational, and political) for distinguishing true from false prophets and for judging whether extraordinary events are genuine miracles. Emphasises tests of doctrine, fulfillment of predictions, natural-explanation elimination, and deference to lawful ecclesiastical/civil authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the probability of a pretended prophet's calling
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing that visions, dreams, and extraordinary gifts may proceed either from God or from natural/second causes, there is need of reason and judgement to discern between natural and supernatural gifts; men must be very circumspect and wary before obeying one who pretends to be a Prophet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be suspicious of persons who claim to govern by teaching the way to felicity (ambition and imposture). Test claims by applying reason and the rules God has given (e.g., Deut. 13, 18; 1 John 4). Do not yield obedience to pretended prophets without examination, unless the sovereign has already authorised them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformable doctrine to the sovereign Prophet / established rule
rubrics_metrics.description: One Old Testament rule to know a Prophet was conformity of his doctrine to that which Moses the Sovereign Prophet had taught; in the New Testament the principal mark is preaching that Jesus is the Christ (1 John 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prophet who teaches anything contrary to the doctrine established by God's Lieutenant (the lawful head of the Church/commonwealth) is not to be hearkened to, even if he works wonders. Use the established public doctrine as the primary doctrinal test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecies must be fulfilled (predictive accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prophet's predictions do not come to pass, this is a ground to distrust and disobey him (Deut. 18:22 and related texts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require that foretold events actually occur; lack of fulfillment marks presumptuous speech. When in doubt about whether a reported prophecy occurred, consult lawful authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a miracle (purpose- and cause-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: A miracle is a work of God, besides his operation by the way of Nature, done for making manifest to his elect the mission of an extraordinary minister for their salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two aspects: (1) it is not effected by ordinary/created causes (beyond natural operation), and (2) it is done with the intention of testifying to the mission of a divine messenger. Both the extraordinary cause and the salvific communicative purpose are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles must be rare and without an apprehensible natural cause
rubrics_metrics.description: A true miracle is such that men wonder because it is strange and cannot be imagined to have been done by natural means; if a natural cause is possible or known, the event is not a miracle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess rarity and examine whether natural or human art can produce the effect (examples: rainbows were miraculous when first seen but are no longer miracles once their cause is known). Do not call frequent or explainable events miracles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles are intended to procure credit for God's messengers (their end)
rubrics_metrics.description: The end of miracles is to procure credit to God's messengers, ministers, and prophets so that men may know they are sent by God, and thus to beget or confirm belief (usually in the elect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the purported miracle serves to confirm the messenger's divine mission; miracles unconnected to edification or to verifying a minister's mission are suspect as genuine miracles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require eyewitness verification and careful inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: We must both see a miracle done and use all means possible to consider whether it was really done and whether it is such that no natural cause could produce it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible insist on direct observation and investigation; do not accept mere reports without scrutiny. If only reports exist, consult the lawful Church authority for judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the lawful Head of the Church (God's Lieutenant) in doubtful cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In doubtful cases about miracles or prophets, men are to have recourse to God's Lieutenant — the lawful Head of the Church (and in a commonwealth, the sovereign) — and submit private judgment to public authority when making confessions or acting publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private belief is free, but public confession and obedience should follow the judgment of the lawful ecclesiastical/civil authority. If the Lieutenant declares a prophet false, do not obey; if he approves, obedience is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of imposture, conjurers, and confederacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Many who seem to work wonders do so by natural tricks, artifice, ventriloquism, secret intelligence, or conspiracies of actors and witnesses, and thus deceive the ignorant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the possibility of deception: jugglers, ventriloquists, conjurers, co-conspiring persons, and staged cures can mimic miracles. Investigate human means and motives (e.g., imposture for gain or fame) before attributing an event to God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles may appear differently to different observers (relative assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: What seems a miracle to one man may seem otherwise to another because admiration depends on knowledge and experience; ignorance or superstition makes people see miracles where the learned see natural causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor in observers' knowledge: consult those acquainted with natural causes (astronomers, natural philosophers) to see if the 'miracle' has a natural explanation. Avoid accepting phenomena as miraculous solely because of popular astonishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No created spirit (devil, angel, or other) can produce a true miracle
rubrics_metrics.description: A true miracle must be the effect of the immediate hand of God; no devil, angel, or other created spirit can do a miracle (if it were by independent power it would be non‑God power; if by power given them then it is not immediate divine action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute genuine miracles only to God; purported wonders claimed for spirits or magick should be investigated as natural arts or imposture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate prophets' prophetic power is derivative and limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophecy of subordinate, perpetually-called prophets (e.g., the seventy elders) was done by the Spirit only in the sense of an inclination, gift, or grace derived from the sovereign prophet (Moses); their prophecy was subordinate and subject to the sovereign's authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat subordinate prophets as having authority only insofar as they co-operate with and are appointed by the sovereign prophet; their utterances must be judged relative to that subordinate, appointed role.

rubrics_metrics.name: God may speak by various modes (visions, dreams, lots, angels, Spirit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scripture records God speaking by visions and dreams, by angels, by the Spirit's graces, and at times by the event of lots; these are the ways God declared his will in Scripture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a claim, consider the claimed mode of divine communication and whether it fits scriptural examples and the tests above (doctrine conformity, predictive fulfillment, rarity, lack of natural cause). Do not assume all modes imply equal authority or supernatural immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every prophecy (except of the sovereign prophet) is to be examined by every subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Because there were many false prophets and controversies, every man is bound to make use of his natural reason to apply the rules God has given to discern true from false prophecy; one must beware of obeying prophets at one's own peril.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals should not surrender private responsibility to judge prophetic claims entirely, unless they have already yielded to the sovereign's authority; apply scriptural marks (conformity, fulfillment) and reason when deciding whether to follow a prophet.
